markscheme.html:
A

Let the downward direction be positive. The ball is dropped from rest (v=0 at t=0). It accelerates downwards due to gravity, so its velocity increases linearly with a constant positive slope (acceleration g). Upon hitting the ground, its velocity instantaneously reverses to an upward (negative) direction. As it moves up, it is still accelerating downwards (decelerating), so its velocity increases from a negative value back towards zero with the same constant positive slope g. Graph A is the only option showing a constant positive slope and a velocity reversal.

question.html:
A ball is dropped from rest. The ball hits the ground and bounces back up. Which of the following diagrams shows the variation with time t of the velocity v of the ball?

Options are four v-against-t graphs labelled A-D in the source diagram.

  1. graph option A from source
  2. graph option B from source
  3. graph option C from source
  4. graph option D from source
